steps.title: Welcome!
steps.en:
In this app you learn by speaking. Every day has the same parts: shadowing, phrases, a 3-2-1 talk, a conversation, listening and a review.
Tap the mic to speak English. When you're stuck, tap සිං and say it in Sinhala: the app helps you say it in English.
steps.si:
මෙම යෙදුමේ ඔබ ඉගෙන ගන්නේ කතා කරමින්. සෑම දිනකම එකම කොටස් තියෙනවා: shadowing, වාක්‍ය ඛණ්ඩ, 3-2-1 කතාව, සංවාදයක්, ඇහුම්කන් දීම සහ නැවත බැලීම.
ඉංග්‍රීසියෙන් කතා කරන්න mic එක ඔබන්න. හිරවුණොත් සිං ඔබා සිංහලෙන් කියන්න: යෙදුම එය ඉංග්‍රීසියෙන් කියන්න උදව් කරයි.

sessions.title: Your voice
sessions.why: A quick check that the app hears you well, how fast you understand, and a first try at shadowing.

what.name: Mic check
what.desc: say one sentence; see what the app heard

steps.en:
Your mentor follows your practice to help you improve. He uses these tools:
• Google speech recognition turns your voice into words.
• Google's voices read Sam's and Maya's words aloud.
• Gemini (Google's AI) plays Sam and Maya, checks your answers and plans your next day. Google may use what is sent to Gemini to improve its services.
• Claude (an AI assistant) helps your mentor read your practice, find problems and make the app better.
The text of your talks goes to your mentor and these tools. Your voice recordings stay on this phone.

steps.title: When you don't catch something, ask!
steps.en:
Never go silent. Ask in English:
• Too fast: "Sorry, could you slow down a bit?"
• Didn't catch it: "Sorry, I didn't catch that."
• One word: "Sorry, what does ___ mean?"
• Hear it again: "Again, please." / "One more time?"
Asking is a good conversation skill. It never loses points.
steps.si:
කවදාවත් නිශ්ශබ්ද වෙන්න එපා. ඉංග්‍රීසියෙන් අහන්න:
• වේගවත් නම්: "Sorry, could you slow down a bit?"
• ඇහුණේ නැත්නම්: "Sorry, I didn't catch that."
• එක වචනයක්: "Sorry, what does ___ mean?"
• නැවත අහන්න: "Again, please."

steps.title: Today's phrases
steps.en:
Six blocks to talk about yourself:
• I'm from… (your home town)
• I live in… (where you live now)
• At the moment I'm… (studying, working, looking for a job)
• I'm really into… (something you love)
• To be honest… (before a true feeling)
• How about you? (always hand it back)

steps.title: Sam's big family lunch
steps.script: So last Sunday was crazy. My aunt came from Kurunegala with her whole family, so we were sixteen people in our small house! My mum cooked from six in the morning: rice, chicken curry, dhal, and of course her famous pol sambol. My little brothers had to sit on the floor because there weren't enough chairs. My uncle is the kind of person who tells the same joke every time, and everyone laughs anyway. After lunch we all watched the cricket match together, and when Sri Lanka won, my grandfather danced! It was noisy and tiring, but honestly, it was the best day this month.

steps.title: Today's phrases
steps.en:
React first, then answer. When you need time, say it out loud instead of going silent:
• Really? / Oh no! / That's great! (react)
• Let me think… / How can I put it… (buy time)
• Well, actually… (start an answer)
• That's a good question. (more time)
steps.si:
මුලින්ම ප්‍රතිචාර දක්වන්න, ඊට පස්සේ පිළිතුරු දෙන්න. වෙලාව ඕනේ නම් නිශ්ශබ්ද වෙනවා වෙනුවට එය කියන්න:
• Really? / Oh no! / That's great!
• Let me think… / How can I put it… (හිතන්න වෙලාව)
• Well, actually… (පිළිතුර පටන් ගන්න)
• That's a good question.

steps.brief: Phone him with three pieces of news, one at a time: you got a pay rise at the café (good), your phone screen broke (bad), your cousin is getting married next month (surprise). Let him react and ask before you give the next one. Ask him one hard question so he must buy time.

steps.title: Sam's three pieces of news
steps.script: Okay, three things happened this week. First, the good news: my mum had a baby last night! I've got a new little brother. His name is Thenuka, and he's so tiny! Second, the bad news: on the way to the hospital I dropped my phone in a puddle, and now the screen is completely black. My mum says it's karma. And third, the strange news: my neighbour's dog followed me to college on Wednesday, and he sat outside the classroom all morning. The teacher thought it was my dog! So, yeah, a busy week.

steps.title: Maya's trip to Kandy
steps.script: Last weekend I finally went to Kandy. I took the early train from Colombo, and it took about three hours, but the views were amazing. First I walked around the lake. There are so many monkeys there! Then I visited the Temple of the Tooth, which was really peaceful. For lunch, a man at the market told me about a small place near the clock tower, and they had the best kottu I've ever had. In the evening it started raining, so I sat in a café and watched the people. It's a bit busy, but I'd love to go back.

steps.title: Two friends meet after years
steps.script: Yesterday something lovely happened. I was waiting for the bus in Pettah when a man said, "Maya? Is that you?" It was Dilan, my best friend from school! We hadn't seen each other for eight years. He looks so different now: he has a beard and he's much taller. He told me he works as a nurse in a big hospital, and he's getting married in March. We were so busy talking that I missed my bus, and then the next one too! In the end we had tea together, and he invited me to the wedding. Anyway, we promised to meet every month.
